title: The Greatness of Their Love
note: The man and then the woman each say how great their love is. It follows the chapters on union and on her beauty, because such love arises from those.

couplets.plain: The moisture that wells at the white teeth of this soft-spoken woman is like milk mixed with honey.
couplets.pm: The moisture that wells at the white teeth of this soft-spoken woman is like milk and honey mixed, and has their taste. Milk and honey each have a known taste, but mixed they make a sweetness no one can name. So it is with this moisture.
couplets.context: At the end of their first union, he tells her how much he wants her.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: Tastes the moisture of her mouth as milk and honey mixed together.

couplets.plain: The bond between this woman and me is the bond between body and soul.
couplets.pm: Whatever the ties between body and soul, such are the ties between this woman and me. They have been blended from the first, share joy and pain alike, and can’t do without each other. Their union was the gods’ work, so she knew nothing of it then. Now she wonders who he is, whether he loves her, and if they will meet again. He reads this in her and answers.
couplets.context: He speaks of the fear of parting.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: the bond between body and soul

couplets.plain: Little figure in the black of my eye, go away. There is no room for the woman I love, with her lovely forehead.
couplets.pm: Figure who lives in the black of my eye, come out of there. If you stay, the woman of the lovely forehead I love has nowhere to live. I can’t bear not seeing her, so she can’t go outside and must live in my eye. There isn’t room for both of you, so give your place to her, who is better than you, and go.
couplets.context: They have met again at the same place. As she leaves him, he says this.
couplets.speaker: he

couplets.plain: This woman in choice jewels is life to the soul, and when she leaves, she is death to it.
couplets.pm: When we join, this woman of choice jewels is to me what living in the body is to the soul. When we part, she is what leaving the body is to it. Life stays at one with you, and dying brings pain, so he compares their union and parting to these.
couplets.context: He has been with her at their daytime meeting place and says this as he leaves.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: Treats a lover’s absence as death.

links.quote: when she leaves, she is death to it

couplets.plain: I would remember, if I ever forgot. But I don’t know how to forget the ways of this woman with her bright, warring eyes.
couplets.pm: If I forgot the qualities of this woman, whose bright eyes wage war, I would think of them. I never forget, so I never need to recall. Her qualities are modesty, innocence, fear and recoiling from any other touch. The man’s words end here, and from now on she speaks.
couplets.context: He has been away and has come back. Her friend asks whether he even thought of them, and he answers.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: I don’t know how to forget

couplets.plain: My lover won’t leave my eyes, and when I blink it doesn’t hurt him. That is how subtle he is.
couplets.pm: Let others think he has gone far because they can’t see him. My lover never leaves my eyes. If I blink without noticing, that doesn’t trouble him. So he is too fine to be seen. Unbroken thought of him has ripened until he is always before her, even when she blinks.
couplets.context: He is away for a while. Afraid her friend will speak ill of him, she says this to herself where her friend can hear.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: My lover lives in my eyes, so I don’t even line them with kohl. I know he would be hidden.
couplets.pm: My lover is always inside my eyes, so I don’t even put kohl on them, knowing he would be hidden for that long. The unspoken point: how can anyone think he has left me, when I see him without a break?
couplets.context: She goes on, to herself, where her friend can hear.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: My lover lives in my heart, so I’m afraid to eat anything hot. I know he would burn.
couplets.pm: My lover is inside my heart, so I fear eating hot food, knowing the heat would reach him. The unspoken point: how can anyone think he has left me, when he is always in my heart?
couplets.context: She goes on, to herself, where her friend can hear.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: I know that if I blink he will be hidden. For just that, this town calls him a stranger.
couplets.pm: Knowing that my lover inside would be hidden if my eyes blinked, I don’t blink. For that much, the town says he has given me the sickness of no sleep and has no loving-kindness. She is hurt that her friend doesn’t understand, so she says “this town” to set her apart. Don’t blame one who has never left.
couplets.context: He has gone, promising to return. To help her bear it her friend speaks ill of him, and she takes his side.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: this town calls him a stranger
links.reason: The town takes her unblinking devotion as proof that he is a stranger to her.

couplets.plain: He lives happily in my heart, always. This town says he lives apart from me, a stranger.
couplets.pm: My lover always lives gladly in my heart. Not knowing this, the town says he lives away from me and has no loving-kindness. By “gladly” she shows that he has it. Don’t blame one who has neither left nor lost his loving-kindness.
couplets.context: She goes on, taking his side against her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: This town says he lives apart from me
